Its four vertices have six pairwise edges and every pair shares a face, so the lesson's polyhedron diagonal count is zero.

perExercise.derivation: AB and FE are the parallel bases of the isosceles trapezoid. Feet H,K on AB have AH=BK=a/4 and height h=sqrt(3)a/4. The perpendicular-plane premise makes h the height over ABC. Inclination satisfies sin(alpha)=h/(a/2). With L on CD directly across the square from H, HL=a and tan(beta)=h/a. The five face areas are a², 3sqrt(3)a²/16, 3sqrt(19)a²/16, a²/4 and a²/4. Sum gives the stated area, unchanged by unfolding.
